paragraphs: I started in civil engineering, where the job was to inspect a structure and say whether it matched the drawing — and to prove it with a log. That habit never left. As an operations manager I built the Excel tracking system that gave a ₦5–6 million monthly business real visibility into inventory, wastage and performance.

Then I learned to build software properly: a six-month certified programme at TS Academy, followed by leading a 12-person team through a full-stack recruitment platform — React front end, Node.js and Express APIs, MongoDB, JWT authentication and role-based access, deployed on Vercel and Render. I have shipped a banking app and an e-commerce store the same way.

Today I combine both: I evaluate AI agent output for rigour, calibration and clarity — the skill Mercor's Introduction to Agents course tests — and I keep trading proprietary capital, five years and 10,000+ hours in. Trading is where I learned to write down what I expected, what happened, and why the difference occurred. It is the same discipline an evaluation rubric asks for.

projects.title: PropFirm Intelligence
projects.oneLiner: Evidence-based prop-firm matching and trading-history analysis, built because I was tired of choosing firms on marketing copy.
projects.body: A local-first Next.js application. Import a closed-trade CSV and it computes net P&L, win rate, profit factor, expectancy, payoff ratio, streaks, per-instrument and per-weekday breakdowns and drawdown — then matches your style against 27 researched account programmes from FTMO, FundedNext, The5ers and BrightFunded. Every stored rule carries its own source URL and verification date, and unknowns are labelled unverified instead of guessed. Files are parsed in the browser tab; nothing is uploaded.
metrics: 27 firm programmes catalogued across 4 firms, each rule sourced and dated
CSV import validated for up to 10,000 trades with duplicate and invalid-row review

faq.q: Are you available for remote work with international teams?
faq.a: Yes. I work from Abuja (WAT, UTC+1) with reliable high-speed internet, a backup line and a flexible schedule. I can overlap with UK/EU mornings and shift earlier for US Eastern teams.

faq.q: What kind of AI evaluation work have you done?
faq.a: I completed Mercor's Introduction to Agents course (certificate MRC-2026-HKHJULZA), which trains and tests rubric-based evaluation of agent output: rigour, calibration and written clarity. Because I build and debug JavaScript, React and Node.js applications, I can also review code and technical output rather than only prose.

JavaScript and TypeScript, React with JSX and React Router, Vite, Node.js with Express and REST APIs, MongoDB with Mongoose, JWT authentication, bcrypt hashing and role-based access control. I deploy to Vercel and Render and manage everything through Git and GitHub.

I have traded proprietary capital for five years with 10,000+ hours logged and have passed 7+ firm evaluations at 1–2% risk per trade. On this site I publish a specific, dated 100-trade sample with its method and its losing streaks rather than a headline claim.

faq.q: Do you take contracts, full-time roles, or both?
faq.a: [CONFIRM — e.g. Both. I take part-time evaluation and development contracts now, and I am open to a full-time remote role with the right team.]
[CONFIRM — e.g. Within 24 hours on weekdays, usually much faster.]
